assertions.interpretation: The era of Yao and Shun is invoked as a past golden-age precedent within the emperor's question.
Zhou Boren (Zhou Yi) held the office of Puye (Vice Director) at the time of the scene.
Zhou Boren then spoke in a stern voice — a sequential event within the scene.
Liu Xiaobiao's annotation notes that Zhou was actually killed by Wang Dun, contradicting the main text's account — background context about Zhou's eventual fate.
The annotation notes that before Emperor Ming ascended the throne, Zhou Yi had already held his office — a chronological correction placing Zhou's appointment before the emperor's reign.

assertion.interpretation: The emperor became furious, returned inside, wrote an edict filling a yellow sheet, handed it to the Tingwei to arrest Zhou, and intended to kill him — sequential events following Zhou's outburst.

The assembled ministers went to visit Zhou after his release — part of the later outcome sequence.
